name: Invention & Origins
blurb: From Niépce's first fixed image to the daguerreotype and the calotype — photography is invented and races to capture portraits, landscapes and the wider world.

name: Pictorialism
blurb: The first movement to argue photography was fine art. Soft focus, hand-working of prints and painterly atmosphere aimed to rival painting and etching.

name: Straight Photography & Modernism
blurb: A reaction against Pictorialism: sharp focus, full tonal range and the unmanipulated frame. Photography asserts its own modern, mechanical vision.

name: Documentary & Social Realism
blurb: The camera as witness and reformer — from Atget's vanishing Paris and Hine's child labourers to the Farm Security Administration's portrait of Depression-era America.

name: Street Photography
blurb: The decisive moment in public space — candid, fast and intuitive, finding form and feeling in the unscripted life of the city.

name: The New Color
blurb: Colour, long dismissed as commercial, is claimed for serious art — the saturated, deadpan vernacular of everyday America.

name: New Topographics
blurb: Stark, unromantic views of the man-altered landscape — parking lots, tract housing and industrial edges replace the sublime wilderness.

name: Staged & Contemporary Surrealism
blurb: Photography as fiction — constructed, cinematic and psychological. Self-portraiture and elaborate set-building turn the frame into a dream or a stage.

name: Contemporary & Digital
blurb: The medium in the new century — large-format tableaux, the deadpan digital sublime, staged psychological fictions and the self-portrait reborn on the social web. Photography becomes vast, constructed and screen-native.
